items.prompt: In a merchant price synchronization system, a catalog operator must publish a price revision. the new price must be visible to checkout without accepting an obsolete version The design review focuses on authentication, sessions, and token boundaries. The normal path is healthy and the design must show where the decision belongs. What is the best primary architecture decision?
constraints: the new price must be visible to checkout without accepting an obsolete version
Choose the mechanism that directly satisfies the stated contract before adding adjacent controls.
The primary decision is separate authentication, session lifecycle, and token validation at the trust boundary..
Keep the scenario provider-neutral and do not rely on a canonical product solution.

options.text: Separate authentication, session lifecycle, and token validation at the trust boundary. In this normal path for merchant price synchronization, a verified identity and a live session are different facts with different revocation and expiry behavior. The owner must also make a stale or partially applied price observable rather than silently passing it to another layer.
Choose the nearest familiar component and let each caller decide authentication, sessions, and token boundaries independently, without a shared owner or failure contract.
Add replication, caching, retries, or asynchronous buffering immediately, even though the scenario has not shown that mechanism is the limiting constraint.
Keep the happy path and treat a stale or partially applied price as an operational exception that the caller can resolve manually.
Select a named cloud or vendor product first and infer the workload, ownership, and guarantee from that product's defaults.

feedback.Reason: Separate authentication, session lifecycle, and token validation at the trust boundary. It addresses the new price must be visible to checkout without accepting an obsolete version through an explicit mechanism and keeps a stale or partially applied price inside a visible ownership and recovery boundary.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: A verified identity and a live session are different facts with different revocation and expiry behavior. The applicability case makes the enforcement point explicit instead of relying on a product default.
Details.scenarioApplication: For merchant price synchronization, the decision keeps the new price must be visible to checkout without accepting an obsolete version attached to the owner that can observe the state. The design treats a stale or partially applied price as a named failure path.
Details.errorCorrection: The distractors either make the boundary unowned, add unmeasured complexity, ignore recovery, or replace mechanism reasoning with provider trivia. Choose the mechanism that directly satisfies the stated contract before adding adjacent controls.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Do not reduce “Authentication, sessions, and token boundaries” to terminology recall. Authentication is not authorization, encryption is not isolation, and client-side controls are not enforcement; define explicit trust boundaries. The trade-off is that explicit ownership and evidence may require a narrower contract or an operational signal, but that cost is preferable to silently violating the stated guarantee.
Details.ownership: The service or boundary that owns the relevant state and can enforce authentication, sessions, and token boundaries must own the decision; callers coordinate through the contract.
Details.transfer: Carry the ownership and failure rule into a new domain, then re-check the changed workload, guarantee, and recovery requirement.
Details.provenance: Technical claim anchored to Building Secure and Reliable Systems (https://google.github.io/building-secure-and-reliable-systems/raw/toc.html); scenario, options, and feedback are independently authored.

items.prompt: In a document processing system, a processing coordinator must submit an extraction job. a retry must not create two billable or irreversible side effects The design review focuses on authentication, sessions, and token boundaries. The same mechanism appears in a different domain with one constraint changed. What is the best primary architecture decision?
constraints: a retry must not create two billable or irreversible side effects
Transfer the ownership and failure rule, then re-evaluate the changed workload rather than copying a product solution.
The primary decision is separate authentication, session lifecycle, and token validation at the trust boundary..
Keep the scenario provider-neutral and do not rely on a canonical product solution.

options.text: Separate authentication, session lifecycle, and token validation at the trust boundary. In this transfer case for document processing, a verified identity and a live session are different facts with different revocation and expiry behavior. The owner must also make a worker retry after an unknown result observable rather than silently passing it to another layer.
Choose the nearest familiar component and let each caller decide authentication, sessions, and token boundaries independently, without a shared owner or failure contract.
Add replication, caching, retries, or asynchronous buffering immediately, even though the scenario has not shown that mechanism is the limiting constraint.
Keep the happy path and treat a worker retry after an unknown result as an operational exception that the caller can resolve manually.
Select a named cloud or vendor product first and infer the workload, ownership, and guarantee from that product's defaults.

feedback.Reason: Separate authentication, session lifecycle, and token validation at the trust boundary. It addresses a retry must not create two billable or irreversible side effects through an explicit mechanism and keeps a worker retry after an unknown result inside a visible ownership and recovery boundary.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: A verified identity and a live session are different facts with different revocation and expiry behavior. The transfer case makes the enforcement point explicit instead of relying on a product default.
Details.scenarioApplication: For document processing, the decision keeps a retry must not create two billable or irreversible side effects attached to the owner that can observe the state. The design treats a worker retry after an unknown result as a named failure path.
Details.errorCorrection: The distractors either make the boundary unowned, add unmeasured complexity, ignore recovery, or replace mechanism reasoning with provider trivia. Transfer the ownership and failure rule, then re-evaluate the changed workload rather than copying a product solution.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Do not reduce “Authentication, sessions, and token boundaries” to terminology recall. Authentication is not authorization, encryption is not isolation, and client-side controls are not enforcement; define explicit trust boundaries. The trade-off is that explicit ownership and evidence may require a narrower contract or an operational signal, but that cost is preferable to silently violating the stated guarantee.
Details.ownership: The service or boundary that owns the relevant state and can enforce authentication, sessions, and token boundaries must own the decision; callers coordinate through the contract.
Details.transfer: Carry the ownership and failure rule into a new domain, then re-check the changed workload, guarantee, and recovery requirement.
Details.provenance: Technical claim anchored to Building Secure and Reliable Systems (https://google.github.io/building-secure-and-reliable-systems/raw/toc.html); scenario, options, and feedback are independently authored.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.unowned_shortcut: It leaves authentication, sessions, and token boundaries dependent on caller discipline instead of placing the decision with the boundary that can enforce it.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.unbounded_scale: The extra mechanism may change consistency, duplicate work, or recovery behavior without addressing the decisive requirement.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.ignore_failure: A design answer must state what the user sees and who owns recovery when a worker retry after an unknown result occurs.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.provider_trivia: The architecture decision should survive a provider change; the mechanism and contract matter more than a product label.
